newsitem.title: USA: NY Gov sees cut in 1997 unemployment insurance tax.
newsitem.headline: NY Gov sees cut in 1997 unemployment insurance tax.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki said Monday that 65 percent of the state's employers will get the benefit of an $85 million drop in unemployment insurance taxes due to the growing economy.
"The success we have achieved in improving New York's business climate means 280,000 employers of all sizes will share in this tax cut during the coming year," he said in prepared remarks.

Labor Commissioner John Sweeney said the state's unemployment insurance trust fund was projected to end calender year 1996 with a balance of around $455 million. The trust fund, which took in about $2.2 billion in 1996, is subsidized by employer payroll taxes.
The commissioner, saying the tax reduction marked a turnaround, assailed the Cuomo Administration for its handling of the economy.

"Previously, we had to borrow from the federal government to meet unemployment insurance benefit obligations because of the economic problems resulting from the policies of the previous adminstration," he said, in prepared remarks.

Pataki said the department's re-employment and fraud control efforts, which started in early 1995, contributed to the tax cut for 1997. Employers qualify for the tax cut based on several factors, including their track record in paying benefits.
